name: cloud-comms
description: Cloud-Comms — constellation of three minimally-forked upstream comms apps (FairEmail / Mattermost mobile / Element X) plus a thin original hub APK. The hub switches between the forks and brokers their data to Cloud-SuperApp over signature-gated AIDL + ContentProvider IPC. Forks are declarative: pinned upstream tag + committed patch series, materialized into gitignored tracker clones at build time. Built via Nix devShell (gradle + AGP + Android SDK + node for the React-Native fork).

android._doc: Hub-only application coordinates. The forks carry their OWN applicationId / version (declared per fork in forks/<x>/build.json) — they are separate APKs.
android._doc_abi_filters: Hub is pure-JVM (no native libs) so ABI filtering is irrelevant to it; kept for schema parity with ea_cloud-superapp. The forks declare their own abi_filters.

signing._doc: Stable SHARED Cloud-constellation signing key — the same key signs SuperApp / Cloud-Nav / Cloud-Comms / Cloud-IDE so cross-app installs + the in-app updater never hit a signature mismatch. The keystore (raw credential) + passwords live ONLY in vault; only these non-secret path refs are here. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/vault) + sops-decrypts vault_secrets, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE / ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD / ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS / ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. Without the vault key (pure-local dev) gradle falls back to the legacy debug keystore. Paths relative to the vault repo root.
signing._disabled_2026_06_24: vault/shared-key signing DISABLED — it signed OU=Cloud Constellation (wrong key c0f94b17), poisoned GHCR and broke installs on every device. Empty vault_keystore => _resolve_signing returns early => legacy per-app keystore (the canonical published key). Do NOT restore without a deliberate full re-key + one-time reinstall on every device.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Mirrors ea_cloud-superapp's pins so the two Android projects share one toolchain story. Node is added for the Mattermost React-Native fork's Metro/JS build.

ipc._doc: Single source of truth for the on-device IPC surface. Kotlin constants in hub + SuperApp + every fork exporter MUST mirror this; contract/comms-ipc-v1.json carries the full table/aidl shapes and is validated by `./build.sh verify-contract`. Bumping `version` is a breaking change — add a comms-ipc-v2.json, never edit v1 in place.

modules._doc: Gradle module graph — settings.gradle iterates this (FIRE rule 6: never hardcode the list). Only the hub is an in-tree gradle module; the three forks are SEPARATE gradle projects living in their materialized tracker clones, built via `./build.sh build-fork <name>`, never included here.

hub.comment: Thin switcher + IPC broker. Original code (no upstream). Declares the signature permission, the unified CommsProvider (reads), the ICommsService AIDL (actions + push callbacks), and the launcher switcher UI.

forks._doc: Declarative fork registry — THE source of truth for the constellation. Each fork = pinned upstream tag + committed patch series under forks/<key>/patches/. `./build.sh materialize-fork <key>` clones the upstream at the pin into the tracker dir, applies the series, and leaves a buildable project. Upstream bump = edit pinned_tag, re-apply, resolve rejects, commit. NEVER a long-lived divergent clone. order: 'priority' is build/dev sequencing only.

mail.label: Cloud Mail (Fairmail)

build._doc: How build-fork builds this fork: gradle task run via the fork's OWN wrapper (FairEmail pins Gradle 9.4.1 / AGP 9.2.1 — never our devShell gradle), glob of the output APK, and signing='keystore_properties' meaning the engine writes keystore.properties at the fork root from the comms keystore (FairEmail's signingConfigs.release reads it natively — zero signing patch).

mail._patches_doc: Informational manifest of the applied series (lexical order). The build engine's source of truth is the glob of forks/mail/patches/*.patch in build.sh::step_materialize_fork — this array mirrors that dir for human/review visibility and MUST be kept in sync when patches are added.
mail.comment: FairEmail. Reuses the EXISTING ea_mail-fairmail tracker clone already used by ea_cloud-superapp's cherry-pick — materialize-fork checks out the pin, never trusts the tracker HEAD. Server: Maddy + Stalwart on oci-mail (imap./smtps. via SNI on :443, jmap.). Do this fork first: pure Java, no RN/Rust, mail server is live.

chat.label: Chat (Mattermost)
chat.comment: Mattermost mobile (React Native). Server: chat.diegonmarcos.com on oci-apps. Exporter is a NATIVE Kotlin module reading WatermelonDB; RN side left untouched. OPEN DECISION before building: push notifications (self-host mattermost-push-proxy as a new cloud service vs sync-on-open + ntfy) — needs owner sign-off.

upstream_apk._doc: Pinned UPSTREAM RELEASE APK — bundle fallback (owner directive 2026-06-12: ALL apps ship inside the hub NOW). bundle-forks embeds this sha256-verified APK whenever our own fork image isn't on GHCR yet; the patched fork replaces it the moment its CI lands. resign=true → the engine zipalign+apksigner's it with the constellation key (Mattermost publishes unsigned APKs — unsigned can't install; our key also makes it IPC-compatible).

matrix.label: Messenger (Element)
matrix.comment: Element X Android (Kotlin + Rust matrix-sdk FFI). BLOCKED until the continuwuity + mautrix-whatsapp + element stack ships (cloud repo, merged 2026-06-10, not deployed). Exporter reads via the Rust-SDK Kotlin BINDINGS, never raw store files. Push via UnifiedPush with our ntfy (rss.diegonmarcos.com) as distributor — Element X supports it natively.

upstream_apk._doc: Pinned UPSTREAM RELEASE APK — bundle fallback (owner directive 2026-06-12: ALL apps ship inside the hub NOW). bundle-forks embeds this sha256-verified APK whenever our own fork image isn't on GHCR yet; the patched fork replaces it the moment its CI lands. resign=true → the engine zipalign+apksigner's it with the constellation key (Mattermost publishes unsigned APKs — unsigned can't install; our key also makes it IPC-compatible). NOTE: blocked_on gates OUR fork build (homeserver work), not stock-client bundling — Element X is a generic Matrix client.

abi_variants._doc: Per-ABI upstream assets. bundle-forks picks abi_variants[$COMMS_BUNDLE_ABI] when set (default arm64-v8a uses the top-level url/sha256). x86_64 = Waydroid debug builds.

dialer.label: Dialer (Fossy)

build._doc: Fossify Phone (the maintained Simple Dialer fork). gradle_task/apk_glob are the foss flavor best-guess — the fork CI build (workflow_dispatch fork=dialer) is the tester; adjust here on first red run. No comms-server endpoint: it is the device Dialer, linked from Cloud-SuperApp Suite>Communications.

call_screening._doc: OWNER DIRECTIVE (default config): the CallScreeningService patch (ROLE_CALL_SCREENING) MUST default to 'contacts_only' — any incoming call whose number is NOT in the device contacts is silently rejected (disallowed, no ring, no missed-call notification); numbers that resolve to a saved contact ring normally. This is the FIRST-RUN DEFAULT baked into the patch's default SharedPreference; the user can change it in-app once the screening settings UI lands. The patch reads this block as its contract — keep code default == default_mode here.
call_screening.rationale: Spam/robocall defence by default — unknown numbers can't ring the phone unless the caller is a saved contact.

dialer.comment: Fossify Phone = the 'Dialer' entry under Cloud-SuperApp Suite/Cloud#Communications. Same constellation patches as the others when forked: branding (com.diegonmarcos.comms.dialer), icon-less + OPEN action, constellation top bar. PLUS a CallScreeningService patch defaulting to contacts-only (see call_screening above). No exporter (a dialer exposes no comms tables); the hub fleet/bundle/updater handle it purely via this registry entry.

upstream_apk._doc: Pinned UPSTREAM RELEASE APK — bundle fallback (owner directive 2026-06-12: ALL apps ship inside the hub NOW). bundle-forks embeds this sha256-verified APK whenever our own fork image isn't on GHCR yet; the patched fork replaces it the moment its CI lands. resign=true → the engine zipalign+apksigner's it with the constellation key (Mattermost publishes unsigned APKs — unsigned can't install; our key also makes it IPC-compatible).

release._doc: Per-APK distribution for the HUB — SAME data-driven pattern as ea_cloud-superapp/build.json::release. build.sh oras-push + gh-release read this block; the GHA workflow (1_workflows/src/cicd/ship-cloud-comms.yml) only invokes those engine commands, no hardcoded registry/tag strings. The three forks publish their own OCI artifacts under their own build systems. {sha} → git short sha, {version_name} → android.version_name.

artifact._doc: Path under dist/ to publish. `debug` is the daily-driver build (no ProGuard, real stacktraces, debug keystore) — THE hub app, not a side-by-side variant. asset_name matches `debug` so the engine skips a redundant copy.

ghcr._doc: ORAS push as an OCI artifact (APK is a blob, not a container). One :latest tag plus per-commit sha + per-version tags.

gh_release._doc: GitHub Release attachment. rolling_tag is canonical: one release (default `latest`) the ship workflow overwrites on every main push, so /releases/latest/download/Cloud-Comms-Hub.apk is a stable URL. tag_pattern stays for immutable per-tag releases under a tag push (rolling release publishes alongside).

phone_install._doc: Targets for build.sh phone-install — pulls the hub APK from GHCR via curl+OCI HTTP API (no oras dep; works on aarch64 Termux without a Nix shell) and copies it where an Android file manager can see it. Override per-env via PHONE_TARGET.

auto_update._doc: In-app FLEET updater — read at gradle eval time into BuildConfig, used by the hub's updater package at runtime. SAME data-driven OCI-pull pattern as ea_cloud-superapp/libs:updater, but the hub manages the WHOLE constellation: itself (release.ghcr.image) PLUS each fork (forks.<k>.image). A WorkManager periodic job checks each app's GHCR :tag digest against the installed APK and prompts PackageInstaller on a diff. Forks with no published image yet (404) or blocked_on set are skipped gracefully. registry/namespace are shared with release.ghcr (engine asserts consistency).
auto_update._doc_interval: WorkManager periodic minimum is 15 min. 6h matches typical cadence + spares battery/data.
auto_update._doc_install: 'prompt' uses PackageInstaller with a user-confirmation dialog (only no-root path). 'silent' needs the system updater privilege (F-Droid Privileged Extension) — not used here.
auto_update._doc_abi_tags: Runtime ABI awareness: the in-app updater tries GHCR tag '<tag>-<deviceAbi>' (e.g. latest-x86_64 on Waydroid) before falling back to the universal '<tag>'. publish-fork pushes :latest for universal APKs and :latest-<abi> for ABI-specific builds.

ui._doc: About-page data — same shape as ea_cloud-superapp/build.json::ui. permissions.runtime is COPIED from the superapp catalog so the hub's About → Permissions renders the IDENTICAL row list (superapp parity); perms the hub manifest doesn't declare render live as denied/not-requested.

permissions._doc_roles: Single-holder RoleManager roles surfaced in About>Permissions. The hub can't grant another app a role — the 'Set Default Apps (Phone · Spam)' button deep-links the system Default-Apps picker where the user selects the Fossy dialer fork. expected_holders = our patched id OR the stock bundled id (✓ when the live holder matches).
